spec.description: Unit states, failures, restarts and timers, with per-host process and zombie counts.

spec.title: Failed units by host
spec.description:
Every unit that was failed for at least one scrape in the range.
- `State`: whether it is still failed now.
- `Flaps`: times it entered or left the failed state; 0 is chronic, 1 broke and stayed, a high count fails on every retry.
- `Of Range`: share of the range spent failed; low is a fresh failure, high a long-standing one.
- Mount, device, scope, slice and automount units are excluded by the collector, so `Failed units` above counts more than this lists.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance, name, type) (changes(node_systemd_unit_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="failed"}[$__range]))
and on (instance, name, type) (sum by (instance, name, type) (avg_over_time(node_systemd_unit_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="failed"}[$__range])) > 0)

spec.title: Failed units by name
spec.description: How many of the selected hosts currently have each unit failed. A unit near the top is a fleet-wide condition rather than one host's problem.

spec.title: New failures
spec.description: Units that entered the failed state during the range and are still failed now.

spec.expr:
count(sum by (instance, name) (changes(node_systemd_unit_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="failed"}[$__range])) > 0
and on (instance, name) (sum by (instance, name) (node_systemd_unit_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="failed"}) == 1)) or vector(0)

spec.title: Automatic restarts
spec.description:
Restarts systemd performed under a unit's `Restart=` policy, by host and unit.
- Only service units have the counter.
- A reboot, a manual restart or `systemctl reset-failed` zeroes it, so operator action never appears here.
- `Trend` separates a single burst from a steady crash loop.

spec.expr:
sum by (key) (label_join(sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{instance=~"$hostname"}[$__interval]))
and on (instance, name) (round(sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{instance=~"$hostname"}[$__range]))) > 0), "key", " · ", "name", "instance")) > 0

spec.title: Units
spec.description: Every unit systemd currently has loaded, including the mount, device, scope, slice and automount units that the collector counts but does not itemise.

spec.title: Time since last trigger
spec.description: Age of each timer's last trigger, with the number of times it fired over the range beside it. Timers that never fired are in `Timers · Timers never fired`.

spec.expr: sum by (instance, name) (changes(node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{instance=~"$hostname"}[$__range])) and on (instance, name) (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{instance=~"$hostname"} > 0)

spec.title: Timers never fired
spec.description: Active timers systemd reports no trigger time for, counted by how many of the selected hosts. A timer lands here when the host booted since it was last due.

spec.expr:
count by (name) ((node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{instance=~"$hostname"} == 0)
and on (instance, name) (node_systemd_unit_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="active"} == 1))

spec.title: Timer activity by name
spec.description:
Each timer, how many of the selected hosts have it, and how many times it fired over the range.
- Hosts but no triggers: a period longer than the range, or a stopped timer.
- Triggers but no hosts: fired during the range, since removed or masked.

spec.title: Failed units
spec.description:
Units systemd currently reports as failed.
- Includes the mount, device, scope, slice and automount kinds the collector counts but does not itemise, so this runs higher than the rows in the tables below.

spec.title: Activating
spec.description: Units mid-start. A count that does not fall back to near zero is a unit hanging in `activating`.

One row per host, with the fleet totals in the footer.
- `Units` and `Failed` count every loaded unit, including the kinds the Failures tab cannot itemise.
- `Restarts` is the range total.
- The trend columns are the range history of the number beside them; each row scales to itself, so they show when a count moved, not how the hosts compare.

spec.expr:
round(sum by (instance) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{instance=~"$hostname"}[$__range])))
and on (instance) (sum by (instance) (node_systemd_units{instance=~"$hostname"}))
or (0 * sum by (instance) (node_systemd_units{instance=~"$hostname"}))

sum by (instance) (node_processes_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="Z"})
or (0 * sum by (instance) (node_processes_pids{instance=~"$hostname"}))

sum by (instance) (node_processes_state{instance=~"$hostname", state="Z"})
or (0 * sum by (instance) (node_processes_pids{instance=~"$hostname"}))

spec.title: Auto restarts
spec.description:
Restarts systemd performed itself under a unit's `Restart=` policy.
- A manual `systemctl restart` or `reset-failed` zeroes the counter instead of incrementing it, so operator action never shows up here.
- The total is approximate; `Failures · Automatic restarts` has the exact per-unit figures.

spec.title: Zombie processes
spec.description: Exited children whose parent has not reaped them. They hold a PID each but no memory or CPU; the Hosts tab names the hosts and shows when each one accumulated them.

spec.title: Systemd
